question: What claim about the agency behind this yoginī is at stake in stating that she, named by will, extends to the end of Māyā by supreme will and through the siddhas?
premises: A yoginī named by will is present.
She extends to the end of Māyā.
This occurs by supreme will and by the siddhas.
inference: The yoginī named by will is presented as operating up to the end of Māyā through the agency of the siddhas and supreme will.
uncertainties: The precise syntactic relation between siddhaiḥ and para-icchayā is not unambiguous.
plain_english: The yoginī named by will, by the siddhas and by supreme will, extends to the end of Māyā.
